title: State of Evidence for the Readout Hypothesis-Generation Programme

equations.label: (unnumbered, Sec.1)
equations.section: 1 Purpose and Evidence Coding (Non-collapse rule for the evidence registry)
equations.text: neighboring evidence != formal-variable validation != truth of the integrated theory
equations.meaning: A local empirical result cited as neighboring evidence is not the same as validating a Readout-programme variable, which is not the same as truth of the integrated theory.
Non-collapse: bare graph/logical reachability of a hypothesis is not the same as its structural accessibility.
Non-collapse: how fast a hypothesis is generated is not the same as its quality or epistemic warrant.
Non-collapse: a larger volume of AI-generated hypotheses is not the same as greater epistemic/readout-distinguishable diversity.

equations.label: (unnumbered, Sec.4)
equations.section: 4 What the Literature Jointly Supports ("The stronger Readout chain")
equations.meaning: A chain of non-collapses proposed as a conceptual typing rule, not yet an experimentally established decomposition.
equations.paper_tier: identity (non-collapse) / conceptual typing rule, not yet decomposed

equations.label: (unnumbered, Sec.3.4)
equations.section: 3.4 Stage D: hypothesis timing, usability, and discrimination
equations.meaning: The VIADS study's direct evidence that faster hypothesis generation does not entail higher-quality hypotheses.

equations.section: 3.6 Stage F / 5.2 Paper II: knowledge topology and first passage
equations.text: G1K != G2K => L(tau_U | G1K, Q) != L(tau_U | G2K, Q)
equations.meaning: Still-open directional claim: different knowledge topologies (G1K vs G2K) imply different distributions of first-passage time to a usable hypothesis, under the same question Q.
equations.paper_tier: hypothesis [Open] (Paper II H1-H2, requires randomized content-matched topology experiment)
